confirmed.title: food_par_for() is fed the ECS-loaded colonist count, not the persistent rtsim roster — the exact frame bug this same file already diagnosed and fixed for immigration
confirmed.law: TWO FRAMES COMPARED AS ONE
confirmed.claim: food_par_for(colonists.count() as u32) computes the town's food target from the ECS-loaded colonist count (specs::Storage<Colonist>::count()), not the full persistent population, so any colonist who is off in a far/unloaded chunk or demoted to Simulated is silently excluded from the 'how many mouths' calculation this session's own fix was written to answer.

Compare to the pre-existing fix 30 lines above the immigration block in the SAME function (lines 21955-21966): '★ ROW 50 FIX (review rank 6): COUNT BOTH SIDES OF THE EQUATION IN THE SAME FRAME. `target_pop` comes from the board's houses (every colonist, wherever they are); `roster` came from the ECS join, which holds only colonists currently LOADED. A colonist who walks out to a far chunk, or whose entity is demoted to Simulated, therefore left both a roster hole ... The persistent rtsim record is the population; the ECS is a rendering of part of it.' But the claim overstates novelty/severity to "medium" as if this were an undiscovered regression. It is neither: the introducing commit (bc6ec62ac0, "STRANDING: distance is not connectivity") explicitly names this exact residual risk under its own "STILL NOT EVIDENCED" section, quoting nearly verbatim the reviewer's concern ("if census `stuck` climbs or a body holds one position past 300s, the lateral arm was load-bearing for a trap I could not see") and pre-registers it as falsifier P4. That commit also shows the team measured 0/49 genuine grounded-lateral entrapments over a 14-game-day soak with roster growing 24->51, and explicitly REJECTED the safer-looking `grounded && head_clear` gate because it "would have starved exactly the population this guard exists to protect" — i.e. this is a deliberate, evidence-driven, disclosed tradeoff, not an unnoticed defect. The failure scenario itself is also purely hypothetical ("e.g. a construction/worldgen artifact walls them into a small room") with no concrete reproducer or in-repo evidence that Veloren's building/worldgen ever produces a sealed, doorless, grounded pocket at near-surface height for a jobless colonist — the one documented real case class this exact fix targeted (indoor colonists) is precisely the case being protected, not attacked. killed.title: lift_over_ground samples different lattice points depending on travel direction, so the same physical segment can be lifted one way and not the reverse -- and no test exercises the asymmetric case
refutations: The integer-truncation math is correct in isolation — I hand-verified the reviewer's own numbers (a=(0,0,0),b=(10,0,0),n=8 forward gives x∈{1,2,3,5,6,7,8}; reversed gives x∈{2,3,4,5,7,8,9}) and Rust does truncate toward zero, so `lift_over_ground` genuinely is not reversal-symmetric as a pure function. But the claim's reachability argument fails against the one real caller. `lift_over_ground` has exactly one production call site (bastion_jobs.rs:29558), fed by `tile_route` (line 209), whose A* neighbor set is strictly the four cardinal `Vec2` directions (lines 260-264) over a fixed 6-block tile grid (`tile_center_wpos` = origin + tile*6 + 3, lines 202-204). Every reconstructed path therefore steps tile-to-tile at exactly ±6 in one axis and 0 in the other, so for every shared/repeated 'corridor' segment: span = 6 exactly, n = span.min(8) = 6, and the interpolation multiplier is either 0 or exactly ±i — never truncated, in EITHER direction. That's not a lucky property of the shipped test's specific numbers (a.y=15929,b.y=15935); it's a structural guarantee of the tile grid: every internal trunk-corridor leg is axis-aligned with span==n, so x/y sampling is provably identical (as a set, and in matched order) forward and backward. The only segment in `wps` that can be diagonal/non-exact is the single final leg from the last tile-center to the literal target (`wps.push(target...)`, line ~29551) — but that leg is never itself traversed in reverse by a return trip, since each direction computes its own fresh path to its own distinct target/tile-center pair. So the specific FAILURE SCENARIO as written — "colonist walks A→B across the ground-bump cell... a different colonist routed B→A across the identical physical corridor... reverse sampling lands on a different set of columns that miss the bump" — cannot occur for the trunk-corridor body in this codebase, because that shared body is structurally immune to the described truncation. The claim's own worked example (span=10, needing the n=8 clamp) also does not match any real call-site geometry, which is always span=6.
